jobs.title: Resort Environmental Senior Officer
jobs.description:
Do you want to make a tangible impact on one of Australia's most unique alpine environments?

Alpine Resorts Victoria (ARV) is seeking a Resort Environmental Senior Officer
to help deliver environmental and sustainability initiatives across Mt Buller and Mt Stirling. This year-round role offers a unique combination of field-based environmental management, data analysis, reporting, and community education
, all while working in Victoria's stunning alpine region.

Working closely with the Environmental Manager and Mt Stirling Operations team, you'll help protect and enhance the alpine landscape through environmental monitoring, conservation programs, regulatory compliance, and sustainability initiatives.

What you'll be doing

✅ Deliver environmental programs, including:
Threatened species management
Flora and fauna monitoring
Pest animal and weed control
Waste reduction and circular economy initiatives

✅ Collect, analyse and report on environmental performance data, including:
Energy, water and waste
Emissions and offsets
Compliance and sustainability metrics

✅ Support environmental planning and compliance by:
Reviewing Site Environmental Management Plans
Monitoring permits, certifications and regulatory obligations
Providing environmental advice and recommendations

✅ Coordinate environmental education programs that promote sustainability and environmental awareness across the resort.
✅ Support broader resort operations when required, including working alongside the Mt Stirling Operations, Assets & Operations, and Ski Patrol teams.

About you

We're looking for someone who is passionate about environmental management and enjoys balancing fieldwork with technical analysis.
You'll bring:
At least 2 years' experience delivering environmental programs
Experience in flora and fauna management, native vegetation offsets and/or circular economy initiatives
GIS and spatial data management experience
Strong analytical and environmental reporting skills
Confidence working outdoors in alpine conditions
An Agricultural Chemical User's Permit with 1080 endorsement, or willingness to obtain one

Desirable:

Qualification in Environmental Science, Natural Resource Management, or a related field
Knowledge of environmental regulations relevant to alpine environments
Capable skier/snowboarder and ASPA qualification

Why join ARV?

At Alpine Resorts Victoria, you'll be part of an organisation responsible for managing Victoria's six alpine resorts and protecting some of the state's most significant natural environments. This is an opportunity to build your environmental career while making a genuine contribution to sustainable alpine management.

Ready to apply? Click on the link below.

📅 Applications close: Tuesday 8 September

ARV oversees the management of Victoria's six alpine resorts: Falls Creek, Mt Buller, Mt Hotham, Mt Baw Baw, Mt Stirling and Lake Mountain. Together, these resorts attract more than one million visitors annually and support approximately 10,000 jobs.
Learn more about us at Alpine Resorts Victoria.

ARV is an equal opportunity employer committed to fostering an inclusive and diverse workplace.

Description

Keeping Washington Clean and Evergreen

The Department of Ecology is hiring two Regional Shoreline Compliance/Enforcement Specialists (Environmental Specialist 4)(Two Positions)
within the Shorelands & Environmental Assistance
(SEA) program.

Note:
This is a temporary position that will end on June 30, 2027. T here is potential to extend based on funding availability.

Location Options:

These positions can be based at any of the following duty stations:

Headquarters Office (HQ) in Lacey, WA .
Central Region Office (CRO) in Union Gap, WA .
Northwest Region Office (NWRO) in Shoreline, WA .

One position will be based in NWRO. The other position will be based in either in HQ or CRO. Upon hire, you must live within a commutable distance from the selected duty station.

Note
: If the selected duty station is the Northwest Region Office in Shoreline, the salary will include an additional 5% premium pay due to its location in King County. Salary range: $6068-$8163 per month.

Schedule

This position is eligible for telework and flexible schedule options.
This position requires reporting to the office one day every two weeks.
Schedules are dependent upon position needs and are subject to change.

Application Timeline

Apply by September 15th, 2026
Applications submitted after the date above may not be reviewed unless additional qualified applicants are needed.

Duties

These Regional Shoreline Compliance/Enforcement Specialist positions provide an opportunity for two senior technical experts to advance Ecology’s mission to protect Washington’s shorelines, wetlands, and riparian areas. In these roles, you will assist with regional implementation of the Shoreline Master Program (SMP) audit and technical assistance effort, support the development of a proactive compliance program, and strengthen state–local partnerships that ensure shoreline development achieves no net loss of ecological functions. You will work directly with local governments to evaluate shoreline permits, assess compliance with SMP requirements, improve monitoring systems, and resolve unauthorized activities affecting priority shorelines and riparian environments.

You will serve as regional enforcement specialists, independently developing cases, conducting investigations, preparing formal enforcement documents, and representing Ecology in complex proceedings involving violations of the Shoreline Management Act. Through collaboration with the Shoreline Policy Lead, SMA Compliance Lead, regional counterparts, and the Attorney General’s Office, you will help implement an adaptive feedback loop that improves statewide consistency, reinforces local permitting systems, and strengthens environmental protections.

What You Will Do

Implement the regional SMP audit and technical assistance program, evaluating shoreline permits, monitoring reports, mitigation obligations, and riparian protection measures to ensure consistency with the SMA and local SMPs.
Provide targeted compliance support to local governments, helping develop monitoring processes, evaluation methods, and systematic approaches to track permit effectiveness and ecological performance.
Conduct field verification for priority shoreline projects, confirming as-built conditions, validating monitoring findings, documenting ecological outcomes, and providing follow-up direction to permittees and local partners.
Lead regional shoreline enforcement activities by identifying unauthorized activities, developing defensible case documentation, conducting site investigations, preparing notices of violation and administrative orders, and coordinating enforcement actions with the SEA Program Enforcement Coordinator and the Attorney General’s Office.
Represent Ecology as senior technical experts in enforcement hearings, settlement discussions, and legal proceedings involving complex shoreline violations and high-priority environmental resources.
Serve as project officers for compliance-related grants and agreements, negotiating work elements, tracking deliverables, and ensuring alignment with shoreline protection and SMP improvement goals.
Collaborate closely with regional shoreline planners, headquarters staff, local governments, and tribal, state, and federal partners to ensure consistent implementation of shoreline management requirements and improve overall SMP compliance statewide.
Contribute to development and refinement of statewide shoreline compliance tools, guidance, training, and best practices that support adaptive management and improve long-term ecological outcomes across Washington.

Qualifications

For detailed information on how we calculate experience and responses to other frequently asked questions, please visit our Recruitment website .

Required Qualifications

Nine (9) years of experience and/or education related to the duties of this position, which includes the following:

Shoreline and Environmental Permit Review: Ability to interpret and evaluate shoreline authorizations, permit conditions, mitigation obligations, and riparian protection requirements for consistency with the Shoreline Management Act (SMA) and local Shoreline Master Programs (SMPs).
Compliance Evaluation and Field Verification: Skill in assessing compliance with SMP provisions through document review and site inspections, including verifying as-built conditions, monitoring reports, and ecological performance standards.
Enforcement Case Development: Experience gathering defensible environmental data, documenting violations, preparing enforcement documents (e.g., notices of violation, administrative orders), and coordinating with enforcement leads and legal partners.
Grant and Agreement Administration: Ability to serve as a project officer—developing, negotiating, and monitoring grant or agreement terms, reviewing deliverables, and ensuring alignment with program objectives.
Intergovernmental Coordination: Skill in working effectively with local governments, state and federal partners, tribal entities, and internal regional staff to support consistent and effective implementation of shoreline compliance activities.
Clear and Professional Communication: Ability to communicate technical, regulatory, or enforcement-related information clearly in writing and verbally to varied audiences, including permittees, local partners, and legal representatives.

Education:
Involving a major study in environmental, physical, or one of the natural sciences; environmental or natural science interdisciplinary studies; environmental planning, or an academic discipline related to the duties of the position.

Examples Of How To Qualify

9 years of experience.
8 years of experience AND 30-59 semester or 45-89 quarter college credits.
7 years of experience AND 60-89 semester or 90-134 quarter college credits (Associate’s degree).
6 years of experience AND 90-119 semester or 135-179 quarter college credits.
5 years of experience AND a Bachelor’s degree.
3 years of experience AND a Master’s degree.

Desired Qualifications

Knowledge of regulatory programs and Ecology’s statutory authority under the SMA.
Knowledge of local government roles and responsibilities under the SMA.
Demonstrated understanding of environmental legislation and regulations at the federal, state, and local level.
Demonstrated understanding of complex environmental permitting processes.

Supplemental Information

Ecology does not use the E-Verify system; therefore, we are not eligible to extend STEM Optional Practical Training (OPT). For more information, please visit www.uscis.gov .

Application Process

Ecology seeks diverse applicants: We view diversity, equity, inclusion, and respect through a broad lens including race, ethnicity, class, age, religion, sexual orientation, gender identity, immigration status, military background, language, education, life experience, physical disability, neurodiversity, and intersectional identities. Qualified job seekers from all backgrounds are encouraged to apply.

How To Apply

Click “Apply” at the top of this page. Complete the entire application, including full work history and responses to all supplemental questions, and attach:

Cover letter, describing your interest in and qualifications for this position
Resume

Because we base our selection on the information you provide, it is in your best interest to complete the application thoroughly. A resume will not substitute for the “work experience” section of the application or vice versa. Applications with blank fields or supplemental question responses with comments such as “see resume” may be considered incomplete.

For detailed application information, please visit our Recruitment website.

Description Of Job

The Work Unit:

The Institutions Unit is under the direction of the Deputy Division Director and is responsible for assuring compliance with the requirements of the food laws and sanitation regulations of the State for assisted living residences, swimming pools, child care facilities, and schools. These duties are accomplished through inspections, recall coordination, outbreak investigations, compliance assistance, and compliance assurance; by reviewing registration information, plan review submissions, and other field-generated information for assisted living residences (for retail food regulation compliance), swimming pools, child care facilities, and schools within the State. The school and child care programs are delegated through contracts to Local Public Health Agencies (LPHA). LPHAs conduct inspections and day-to-day program functions at the local level. This unit provides direct service for schools and child care facilities in the absence of a local program. The Division performs program audits and inspection standardization exercises with the delegated LPHAs. The unit, in cooperation with LPHAs, is responsible for assuring compliance with the requirements of the institutional environmental health laws and regulations of the State. The Unit determines the appropriate response, which may include informal or formal inquiries, such as embargo, condemnation, seizure, injunctive relief, and recalls, requesting additional field investigations, recommending and subsequently researching and recommending administrative or judicial enforcement actions, and developing and negotiating assessments. The Unit is also responsible for drafting new regulations, completing State Board of Health documents, and coordinating stakeholder meetings.

What You Will Do

The purpose of this position is to serve as an environmental protection specialist within the school and childcare programs. This position conducts regulatory inspections; prepares inspection reports, compliance advisories, LPHA assessments, and orders or recommendations for enforcement. Additionally, this position serves as a trainer in school and childcare programs. The position conducts training and joint inspections for LPHA staff and develops guidance materials for the programs. In addition to direct facility inspection oversight, this position provides compliance assistance, guidance, and training to the regulated community and local public health agencies. This position is expected to be a junior-level inspector with the goal of being fully operational as a senior-level inspector. This position requires wide-ranging oversight from the supervisor.

Key Responsibilities

Writes technical reports, creates and maintains accurate records, and initiates appropriate enforcement actions such as follow-up inspections, voluntary condemnations, and voluntary closures as necessary when non-compliance is identified within school or childcare operations.
Works collaboratively with epidemiologists to investigate illness and outbreak investigations.
Through research of technical reports, governing regulations, statutory requirements, and other resource materials, creates and drafts responses to questions and inquiries presented by local public health agencies' staff, school administrators, childcare providers, and the public.
Actively monitors progress and reviews reports submitted by LPHAs for completeness and contract requirements.

Or

A combination of related education from an accredited college or university in Biology, Environmental Science for a field of study closely related to the work assignment and One (1) year of experience in a field related to the work assigned to the position, such as environmental health inspections or in an occupation directly related to the work assigned in this position to equal five (5) years.

.

Duties

These Regional Shoreline Compliance/Enforcement Specialist positions provide an opportunity for two senior technical experts to advance Ecology’s mission to protect Washington’s shorelines, wetlands, and riparian areas. In these roles, you will assist with regional implementation of the Shoreline Master Program (SMP) audit and technical assistance effort, support the development of a proactive compliance program, and strengthen state–local partnerships that ensure shoreline development achieves no net loss of ecological functions. You will work directly with local governments to evaluate shoreline permits, assess compliance with SMP requirements, improve monitoring systems, and resolve unauthorized activities affecting priority shorelines and riparian environments.

You will serve as regional enforcement specialists, independently developing cases, conducting investigations, preparing formal enforcement documents, and representing Ecology in complex proceedings involving violations of the Shoreline Management Act. Through collaboration with the Shoreline Policy Lead, SMA Compliance Lead, regional counterparts, and the Attorney General’s Office, you will help implement an adaptive feedback loop that improves statewide consistency, reinforces local permitting systems, and strengthens environmental protections.

What You Will Do

Implement the regional SMP audit and technical assistance program, evaluating shoreline permits, monitoring reports, mitigation obligations, and riparian protection measures to ensure consistency with the SMA and local SMPs.
Provide targeted compliance support to local governments, helping develop monitoring processes, evaluation methods, and systematic approaches to track permit effectiveness and ecological performance.
Conduct field verification for priority shoreline projects, confirming as-built conditions, validating monitoring findings, documenting ecological outcomes, and providing follow-up direction to permittees and local partners.
Lead regional shoreline enforcement activities by identifying unauthorized activities, developing defensible case documentation, conducting site investigations, preparing notices of violation and administrative orders, and coordinating enforcement actions with the SEA Program Enforcement Coordinator and the Attorney General’s Office.
Represent Ecology as senior technical experts in enforcement hearings, settlement discussions, and legal proceedings involving complex shoreline violations and high-priority environmental resources.
Serve as project officers for compliance-related grants and agreements, negotiating work elements, tracking deliverables, and ensuring alignment with shoreline protection and SMP improvement goals.
Collaborate closely with regional shoreline planners, headquarters staff, local governments, and tribal, state, and federal partners to ensure consistent implementation of shoreline management requirements and improve overall SMP compliance statewide.

Qualifications

Required Qualifications

Nine (9) years of experience and/or education related to the duties of this position, which includes the following:

Shoreline and Environmental Permit Review: Ability to interpret and evaluate shoreline authorizations, permit conditions, mitigation obligations, and riparian protection requirements for consistency with the Shoreline Management Act (SMA) and local Shoreline Master Programs (SMPs).
Compliance Evaluation and Field Verification: Skill in assessing compliance with SMP provisions through document review and site inspections, including verifying as-built conditions, monitoring reports, and ecological performance standards.

Grant and Agreement Administration: Ability to serve as a project officer—developing, negotiating, and monitoring grant or agreement terms, reviewing deliverables, and ensuring alignment with program objectives.

Clear and Professional Communication: Ability to communicate technical, regulatory, or enforcement-related information clearly in writing and verbally to varied audiences, including permittees, local partners, and legal representatives.

Company Description
M/s M N Ramesh Engineers & Contractors (MNR E&C) is a civil infrastructure firm with over two decades of experience delivering large-scale water supply and sanitation projects across Karnataka. Established in 2005 and converted to a partnership firm in 2018, the company has expanded its operational capacity while maintaining steady growth. MNR E&C focuses on constructing Water Treatment Plants, Sewage Treatment Plants, Overhead Tanks, wells, and pipeline networks, and executes turnkey integrated water-supply systems for urban and rural regions. The organization is known for its engineering expertise, timely project delivery, and strong adherence to quality and environmental standards. Through major projects for government agencies, MNR E&C contributes to improved water access, sanitation, and sustainable community development across the state.
Role Description
The Environmental Engineer will work full time on-site in Bangalore Urban, supporting the planning, design, and implementation of water and wastewater infrastructure projects. Responsibilities include assessing environmental impacts of construction activities, developing mitigation measures, and ensuring compliance with relevant environmental regulations and standards. The role involves supporting design and operation of wastewater and sewage treatment systems, reviewing project drawings and documentation for environmental considerations, and coordinating with project managers, site engineers, and regulatory authorities. The Environmental Engineer will prepare technical reports, environmental monitoring plans, and compliance documentation, and will support waste management practices on project sites to align with sustainability goals. This position also requires participation in site inspections, data collection, and continuous improvement of environmental performance across projects.
Qualifications

Candidates should possess skills in Environmental Compliance and Environmental Consulting to interpret regulations, advise project teams, and prepare compliance documentation.
Candidates should possess skills in Wastewater Treatment and Waste Management to support design, operation, and optimization of treatment systems and on-site waste handling practices.
Candidates should possess skills in Environmental Impact Assessment to evaluate project impacts, propose mitigation measures, and support approvals from relevant authorities.
Bachelor’s degree or higher in Environmental Engineering, Civil Engineering with an environmental focus, or a related discipline.
Knowledge of national and state-level environmental regulations applicable to water and sanitation infrastructure.
Experience working on water supply, sewage, or sanitation projects, preferably with public infrastructure or government contracts.
Strong analytical, reporting, and documentation skills, with proficiency in relevant engineering and office software tools.
Ability to work collaboratively on-site with multidisciplinary teams and to travel to project locations as required.
